decisionsTitle: The race number's strip draws from the same elevation core as the page: kilometres, altitudes, the aid stations named; the picture's recommended shape
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-16:** on the race number's GPX strip with «Start» and «Sosire» — «I like how it looks when we display from GPX but I want to show the KM & Elevation and hydration points»; of the picture the club may upload instead — «if we choose to put a picture, we need to say what is the aspect ratio recommended for it»; and of the page's new profile — «mi-ar plăcea cumva să refolosesc acel widget … să fie și pe pagină și pe BIB». Amends §750 (the profile's strip), §757 (the checkpoints on it) and §759 (the picture of the profile), and the elevation core's decision of the same day (§802, the one the tick «Arată pe profilul traseului» belongs to).

**Decision — one layout, the core's.** The strip is no longer drawn by the bib's own arithmetic. `bib-profile-strip.ts` asks `routes/elevation/geometry.ts` — the core the event page draws from — once, for the strip's own box (`profileChartWidth` or the whole strip's width, by `profileHeight` 38 points), and both renderers draw the points it returns: `bibs-pdf.ts` as vectors, `bib-image.tsx` as an SVG with the words as boxes set at the core's baselines (`BIB_TEXT_ASCENT`), so the sheet and the picture cannot disagree (a test compares their positions). The bib's own GPX reader (`parseGpxProfile`) is gone: the extras read through the core's `readRouteElevation` and `parseGpxElevation`, one reader and one cache for the page, the editor and the number. The strip now shows: the **kilometre scale** — faint ticks at the foot (1 km up to 12, 2 up to 25, 5 beyond) with their numbers where they fit and «km» once after the last — and the **highest and the lowest altitude** («812 m», above its point; the lowest in the foot row, or beside «Start» or «Sosire» when its point is the start or the finish — a loop's always; only the highest when the two are within five metres); **the pins** the core draws, a ring above the plot with the kind's glyph — a drop, a fork, a cross, a stopwatch, an arrow, a dot — a stem down to the foot and a dot on the line.

**The words.** With «…cu orele limită» off an aid station says what it is — «km 5 · apă», «km 9 · hrană», «km 5 · apă + hrană» — and any other point only «km 12»; with it on, «km 12 · 11:30» as §757, a point without a cut-off «km 12». The crowding rule is §757's, kept: the times go first, all of them (the strip asks the core with the times and, if one label would be dropped, again without them all), then the kilometres where they have room, the end words and the points' words winning over the scale; the core gains one additive option, `clearExtremes`, so the lowest altitude's label shares the foot row with the kilometres without touching them (the kilometres give way to it; the label stands beside the end word it would touch, right of «Start» or left of «Sosire», and gives way to a point's words). Compact mode is not used: it drops the marker labels the bib must keep.

**The tick «Kilometrii și altitudinile pe profil»** (`showProfileScale`): under «Profilul traseului», beside «Punctele de control pe profil», offered with the GPX source only (hidden for a picture, as that one is), **on by default** and for every design saved before the key (`.catch(true)`: a design is JSON, no migration), carried by the design's JSON export and import and by the preview's address like the others. Off, the strip is the line, «Start» and «Sosire» and the pins, as before.

**One meaning for «Arată pe profilul traseului».** The tick the club sets on each point (§802, the core's decision) decides the pin on the page's profile **and** on the race number's: an unticked point stays in the table and on the page and is drawn by neither profile. The card's help sentence now says so («Punctele debifate rămân în tabel și pe pagină; nici profilul paginii, nici cel de pe numărul de concurs nu le desenează.»), where it said the number follows its own setting. The picture's stamp carries the tick (`checkpointsStampPart`, and the desk's `CHECKPOINTS_STAMP`, a «!» after an unticked point), and `BIB_DRAWING_VERSION` goes to 4, so every stamped picture address changes once.

**Pins that would touch.** The page's core never drops a pin (it raises its head to the next row); a strip 38 points tall has one row, so the pins a head's reach (2.5 radii, 8 points) would put over one another are thinned before the core is asked: the first stays, unless the later is an aid station and the earlier is not — §757's rule, kept — and two aid stations that would touch are one pin that says both («km 4 · apă + hrană»), so a water point followed by a food point never reads as «no food here». The highest altitude's label, which stands above its point, moves beside a pin it would cover (or its stem) and is not drawn where there is no room.

**The picture's recommended shape, before the upload.** One rule gives it — `bibProfilePictureRatio(figuresShown)`, the box the picture is fitted whole in (`bibProfileChartWidth`, `profilePictureHeight` 36 points: the picture's own box, which is the row less its one-point margins) — to the crop dialog's «Forma» line and to the sentence the panel prints under the choice «O poză încărcată», beside its upload box: «Recomandat: o imagine lată, întreagă, fără decupaj. Cu cifrele lângă profil: 10,6 la 1, adică 1580 × 150 px la 300 dpi. Fără ele, sau fără cifre de arătat: 14,5 la 1, adică 2180 × 150 px.» — both shapes, so the sentence is true whatever the figures box under it says before a save (it is drawn on the server and the box is not saved yet), the example sizes at `BIB_PICTURE_PRINT_DPI` (300) from the same geometry (`bibProfilePictureExample`), never a number typed in a message.

**Refused.** A second reader of the GPX for the bib (one reader, the core's); drawing the strip with `compact` (it drops the words); dropping pins in the core (the page keeps every pin); an altitude axis down the side of the strip (it has no room, and the figures stand beside it already); the checkpoints' unticked state following a setting of the number's own (one meaning, on every profile).
changelogLine: - **The race number's profile strip draws from the same elevation core as the page** — kilometre ticks and numbers, the highest altitude above its point and the lowest in the foot row (beside «Start» or «Sosire» when it is the start or the finish), pins with a drop, a fork or a cross, the aid stations named («km 5 · apă», «km 9 · hrană», «km 4 · apă + hrană» for two that touch, or «km 12 · 11:30» with the cut-offs), the points unticked «Arată pe profilul traseului» left off the number too; the tick «Kilometrii și altitudinile pe profil» (on by default) turns the scale off; and the designer says the recommended shape of an uploaded picture before the upload. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criteria 78 and 88. Given a design with «Profilul traseului» drawn from the GPX, when a number is printed or previewed, then the strip is laid out once by the shared elevation core in its own box and the sheet and the picture draw the same points — the line and the area, a tick at each kilometre with its number where it fits and «km» after the last, the highest altitude above its point and the lowest in the foot row — beside «Start» or «Sosire» when its point is the start or the finish (only the highest within five metres), «Start» and «Sosire» — with each checkpoint the club ticked «Arată pe profilul traseului» as a ring with the kind's glyph, a stem and a dot on the line and none for an unticked one; the words under a pin are «km 5 · apă», «km 9 · hrană», «km 12» and, with «…cu orele limită» and room for every one, «km 12 · 11:30», the end words and the points' words winning over the kilometres; and with «Kilometrii și altitudinile pe profil» unticked (on by default and for every design saved before it, drawn with the GPX only, carried by the design's JSON) the scale and the altitudes are left off and the rest stays (2026-10-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 92. Given the choice «O poză încărcată» in the designer, then before any upload the sentence under the choice says the recommended shape of the picture from the strip's own geometry — «Recomandat: o imagine lată, întreagă, fără decupaj. Cu cifrele lângă profil: 10,6 la 1, adică 1580 × 150 px la 300 dpi. Fără ele, sau fără cifre de arătat: 14,5 la 1, adică 2180 × 150 px» naming both shapes, whatever the figures box says before a save — and the ratio is the one the crop dialog's «Forma» line gives (2026-10-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 140 and the elevation profile's criterion. Given a checkpoint unticked «Arată pe profilul traseului», then neither the event page's profile nor the race number's strip draws it, the table still lists it, the card says so («Punctele debifate rămân în tabel și pe pagină; nici profilul paginii, nici cel de pe numărul de concurs nu le desenează»), and the bib picture's stamp changes with the tick (2026-10-16, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the race number's strip draws from the same elevation core as the page: kilometres, altitudes, the aid stations named; the picture's recommended shape
